I received my first copy of the UFO Investigator some weeks ago, and enjoyed it immensely.
I've shared it around to quite a few of my friends, and they appear to be quite impressed,
even though they weren't UFO believers.
I think the most impressive thing about the publication is the obviously high standard
and high qualification of the members of the Board of Governors.
I think that will go a long way to crediting the UFO subject generally in the eyes of the
public.
I was very interested too to see that you are allocating space each issue for members'
questions.
One particular question I would like to see answered, quite possibly you may already have given space to it in the second issue of the Investigator,
is the very interesting matter which arose in the Flying Saucer Review of England in the last issue about a peculiar sighting in Brazil.
I understand that some sort of substance fell from a flying saucer which was identified as being Puer 10,
tin which could not be found on earth under any circumstances. The report went on to say
that Professor Maney had got hold of a piece of this tin and had analysed it and found
that it was pure tin. There weren't any further details given in the flying saucer review
so I shall look forward to hearing further details as to whether NICAP has made any further
analysis and has any more news to hand. We as a society feel very proud to be
associated with you in this great work and we hope that you'll call on us at
any time that you find that we can be of use to you. Of course if we get any
good sightings here we'll forward them on to you. During the last few months
however, I should point out that we've had very few sightings, very few good
sightings. On May the 19th there was a peculiar incident when a meteor-like object flashed right
across the state and was seen by thousands of people. That was very peculiar. You may have
read about it in the English Flying Source Review. However, since then things have been very quiet.
In 1953-54 we had many reports, they were frequent, almost weekly you might say, of peculiar sightings,
But since then, things have quietened down.
It's almost as though the UFOs had a good look at us in those years,
decided we weren't of military or scientific interest,
and went off to places which were more interesting to them.
At any rate, that's the way it seems to me.
Well, I shan't take up any more of your time,
but I will look forward to getting this tape back from you with your comments recorded on it,
